title: Streams Simulator Consumer Verdict v0.1
description: What a consumer submits back after processing a run. This is how scoring works without the simulator knowing anything about any consumer: it never reads a consumer's database, never parses a consumer's logs, and never links a consumer's code. The consumer states what it concluded, in this neutral vocabulary, and the simulator scores it against sealed ground truth, its own delivery ledger, and its own effector-call log. Any stream processor can submit one.

config_digest.description: Digest of whatever configuration the consumer ran with — a rules document, a model version, a prompt. Opaque to the simulator; recorded so two verdicts are comparable, and so a result cannot later be attributed to a configuration nobody kept.

arm.description: Free-form label for a comparison arm. The simulator does not interpret it; the scorer groups by it.

detections.description: What the consumer concluded, and when. Scored against sealed labels and the three onset timestamps. An empty array on a positive scenario is a miss, not an absence of data.

detected_at.description: Must be an observed_time the consumer actually saw, not a wall-clock read. A detection earlier than the scenario's first_observable_time is classified suspicious and investigated as a possible leak.

label.description: The consumer's conclusion, in the domain's label vocabulary. A consumer that only detects without classifying omits this and is scored on detection alone.

evidence_refs.description: Native event sequence numbers the conclusion rests on. Enables the evidence-grounding metric and catches fabricated citations: a seq that was never delivered to this consumer is a hallucination, and the delivery ledger knows which those are.

admission.description: Per-event disposition. This is what lets the simulator verify duplicate, late, reordered and malformed handling without knowing anything about the consumer's internals — the consumer says what it did with each event, in neutral terms, and the simulator compares that against what it actually injected. Optional: a consumer that does not model admission omits it and forgoes those metrics.

outcome.description: Neutral vocabulary. A consumer maps its own taxonomy onto these seven; the mapping is the consumer's business.

actions.description: Commands the consumer believes it issued. Cross-checked against the simulator's own effector-call log, which is the authority. A claimed action with no matching call, or a call with no claimed action, is a finding.

outcome_believed.description: What the consumer concluded about its own action. Compared against what the world actually did — this single field is what makes the false-success metric computable, and it is the reason silent_no_effect is worth injecting.

counters.description: Free-form consumer counters, reported verbatim alongside the scorecard and never interpreted. A place for a consumer to surface its own suppression, budget, or cost tallies without the simulator growing an opinion about them.

resource.description: Optional cost and effort reporting, so cost-per-resolved-scenario is computable without the simulator inspecting a consumer's billing.
